use std::fmt;

Listing 12.15 Groups and processes, in Go. code/go/cgmodel/main.go

// unlimited is the value of a limit that is written "max" in a control file.
const unlimited = math.MaxInt

var errAgain = errors.New("EAGAIN")

// A group is one node of the hierarchy. pids and memory are the usage of the
// group and of every group below it. refused and oomKills are the counters
// the kernel publishes in pids.events and memory.events.
type group struct {
	name      string
	parent    *group
	children  []*group
	processes []*process

	pidsMax, memoryMax int
	pids, memory       int
	refused, oomKills  int
}

// A process belongs to one group and holds an amount of memory.
type process struct {
	name   string
	home   *group
	memory int
}

// child adds a group below g, with no limits of its own.
func (g *group) child(name string) *group {
	c := &group{name: name, parent: g, pidsMax: unlimited, memoryMax: unlimited}
	g.children = append(g.children, c)

	return c
}

Listing 12.16 Groups and processes, in Rust. code/rust/cgmodel/src/main.rs

/// The value of a limit that is written "max" in a control file.
const UNLIMITED: usize = usize::MAX;

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Again;

impl fmt::Display for Again {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("EAGAIN")
    }
}

/// One node of the hierarchy. `pids` and `memory` are the usage of the group
/// and of every group below it. `refused` and `oom_kills` are the counters
/// the kernel publishes in `pids.events` and `memory.events`.
struct Group {
    parent: Option<usize>,
    pids_max: usize,
    memory_max: usize,
    pids: usize,
    memory: usize,
    refused: usize,
    oom_kills: usize,
}

/// A process belongs to one group and holds an amount of memory.
struct Process {
    name: &'static str,
    home: usize,
    memory: usize,
    alive: bool,
}

/// The hierarchy: groups and processes, referred to by index.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Hierarchy {
    groups: Vec<Group>,
    processes: Vec<Process>,
}

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Adds a group below `parent` and returns its index.
    fn group(&mut self, parent: Option<usize>, pids_max: usize, memory_max: usize) -> usize {
        self.groups.push(Group {
            parent,
            pids_max,
            memory_max,
            pids: 0,
            memory: 0,
            refused: 0,
            oom_kills: 0,
        });

        self.groups.len() - 1
    }

    /// The group itself and every group above it, nearest first.
    fn upward(&self, group: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
        let mut path = vec![group];

        while let Some(parent) = self.groups[path[path.len() - 1]].parent {
            path.push(parent);
        }

        path
    }
}

spawn checks every level before it changes any counter. The refusal is recorded in the group whose limit was reached, which is where the kernel increments pids.events.

Listing 12.17 Starting a process under a hierarchy of limits, in Go. code/go/cgmodel/main.go

// spawn starts a process in g. The process is counted in g and in every
// group above it, so it is refused when any of them is at its limit.
func (g *group) spawn(name string) (*process, error) {
	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		if up.pids == up.pidsMax {
			up.refused++

			return nil, errAgain
		}
	}

	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.pids++
	}

	p := &process{name: name, home: g}
	g.processes = append(g.processes, p)

	return p, nil
}

Listing 12.18 Starting a process under a hierarchy of limits, in Rust. code/rust/cgmodel/src/main.rs

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Starts a process in a group and returns its index. The process is
    /// counted in the group and in every group above it, so it is refused
    /// when any of them is at its limit.
    fn spawn(&mut self, group: usize, name: &'static str) -> Result<usize, Again> {
        let path = self.upward(group);

        for &up in &path {
            if self.groups[up].pids == self.groups[up].pids_max {
                self.groups[up].refused += 1;

                return Err(Again);
            }
        }

        for &up in &path {
            self.groups[up].pids += 1;
        }

        self.processes.push(Process {
            name,
            home: group,
            memory: 0,
            alive: true,
        });

        Ok(self.processes.len() - 1)
    }
}

allocate charges first and then enforces. For each level that is over its limit, it selects the process with the most memory in the subtree of that level. The victim is chosen from the whole subtree, so it can be a process in a different child group from the one that made the allocation.

Listing 12.19 Charging memory, and ending the largest process, in Go. code/go/cgmodel/main.go

// charge adds an amount, which may be negative, to the memory count of a
// group and of every group above it.
func (g *group) charge(amount int) {
	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.memory += amount
	}
}

// allocate gives a process more memory. While a group above the process is
// over its limit, the largest process in that group's subtree is killed. It
// returns the names of the processes killed.
func (p *process) allocate(amount int) []string {
	p.memory += amount
	p.home.charge(amount)

	var killed []string

	for up := p.home; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		for up.memory > up.memoryMax {
			victim := up.largest()
			up.oomKills++
			killed = append(killed, victim.name)
			victim.kill()
		}
	}

	return killed
}

// largest returns the process with the most memory in the subtree of g.
func (g *group) largest() *process {
	var found *process

	for _, p := range g.processes {
		if found == nil || p.memory > found.memory {
			found = p
		}
	}

	for _, c := range g.children {
		if p := c.largest(); p != nil && (found == nil || p.memory > found.memory) {
			found = p
		}
	}

	return found
}

// kill removes a process from its group and returns its memory and its
// place in the process count.
func (p *process) kill() {
	p.home.charge(-p.memory)

	for up := p.home; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.pids--
	}

	for i, other := range p.home.processes {
		if other == p {
			p.home.processes = append(p.home.processes[:i], p.home.processes[i+1:]...)

			break
		}
	}
}

Listing 12.20 Charging memory, and ending the largest process, in Rust. code/rust/cgmodel/src/main.rs

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Gives a process more memory. While a group above the process is over
    /// its limit, the largest process in that group's subtree is killed.
    /// Returns the names of the processes killed.
    fn allocate(&mut self, process: usize, amount: usize) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        let path = self.upward(self.processes[process].home);

        self.processes[process].memory += amount;

        for &up in &path {
            self.groups[up].memory += amount;
        }

        let mut killed = Vec::new();

        for &up in &path {
            while self.groups[up].memory > self.groups[up].memory_max {
                let Some(victim) = self.largest(up) else {
                    break;
                };

                self.groups[up].oom_kills += 1;
                killed.push(self.processes[victim].name);
                self.kill(victim);
            }
        }

        killed
    }

    /// Returns the living process with the most memory in the subtree of a
    /// group.
    fn largest(&self, group: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        (0..self.processes.len())
            .filter(|&p| self.processes[p].alive)
            .filter(|&p| self.upward(self.processes[p].home).contains(&group))
            .max_by_key(|&p| self.processes[p].memory)
    }

    /// Ends a process and returns its memory and its place in the process
    /// count.
    fn kill(&mut self, process: usize) {
        let memory = self.processes[process].memory;

        for up in self.upward(self.processes[process].home) {
            self.groups[up].memory -= memory;
            self.groups[up].pids -= 1;
        }

        self.processes[process].alive = false;
    }
}

Listing 12.21 The trace, in Go. code/go/cgmodel/main.go

func main() {
	team := &group{name: "team", pidsMax: 4, memoryMax: 100}
	jobA, jobB := team.child("job-a"), team.child("job-b")

	var started []*process

	for _, start := range []struct {
		in   *group
		name string
	}{{jobA, "a1"}, {jobA, "a2"}, {jobA, "a3"}, {jobB, "b1"}} {
		p, err := start.in.spawn(start.name)

		if err != nil {
			fmt.Println(err)

			return
		}

		started = append(started, p)
	}

	fmt.Printf("3 processes in job-a and 1 in job-b: pids.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d\n",
		jobA.pids, jobB.pids, team.pids)

	_, err := jobB.spawn("b2")
	fmt.Printf("another process in job-b, team at pids.max 4: %v, pids.events max of team %d\n", err, team.refused)

	a1, b1 := started[0], started[3]

	a1.allocate(60)
	fmt.Printf("a1 allocates 60: memory.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d\n", jobA.memory, jobB.memory, team.memory)

	killed := b1.allocate(50)
	fmt.Printf("b1 allocates 50, team at memory.max 100: killed %v, oom_kill of team %d\n", killed, team.oomKills)
	fmt.Printf("afterwards: memory.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d, pids.current team %d\n",
		jobA.memory, jobB.memory, team.memory, team.pids)
}

Listing 12.22 The trace, in Rust. code/rust/cgmodel/src/main.rs

fn main() -> Result<(), Again> {
    let mut tree = Hierarchy::default();

    let team = tree.group(None, 4, 100);
    let job_a = tree.group(Some(team), UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED);
    let job_b = tree.group(Some(team), UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED);

    let a1 = tree.spawn(job_a, "a1")?;
    tree.spawn(job_a, "a2")?;
    tree.spawn(job_a, "a3")?;
    let b1 = tree.spawn(job_b, "b1")?;

    println!(
        "3 processes in job-a and 1 in job-b: pids.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].pids, tree.groups[job_b].pids, tree.groups[team].pids
    );

    if let Err(error) = tree.spawn(job_b, "b2") {
        println!(
            "another process in job-b, team at pids.max 4: {error}, pids.events max of team {}",
            tree.groups[team].refused
        );
    }

    tree.allocate(a1, 60);
    println!(
        "a1 allocates 60: memory.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].memory, tree.groups[job_b].memory, tree.groups[team].memory
    );

    let killed = tree.allocate(b1, 50);
    println!(
        "b1 allocates 50, team at memory.max 100: killed [{}], oom_kill of team {}",
        killed.join(" "),
        tree.groups[team].oom_kills
    );
    println!(
        "afterwards: memory.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}, pids.current team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].memory,
        tree.groups[job_b].memory,
        tree.groups[team].memory,
        tree.groups[team].pids
    );

    Ok(())
}
3 processes in job-a and 1 in job-b: pids.current job-a 3, job-b 1, team 4
another process in job-b, team at pids.max 4: EAGAIN, pids.events max of team 1
a1 allocates 60: memory.current job-a 60, job-b 0, team 60
b1 allocates 50, team at memory.max 100: killed [a1], oom_kill of team 1
afterwards: memory.current job-a 0, job-b 50, team 50, pids.current team 3
LineWhat it shows
job-a 3, job-b 1, team 4Each process is counted in its own group and in team.
EAGAINjob-b has no limit. The fork is refused by the limit of team.
a1 allocates 60The memory is charged to job-a and to team.
killed [a1]The allocation by b1 puts team over its limit, and the largest process below team is a1, in the other child group.
the last lineAfter the kill, team is within its limit and has 3 processes.

Correspondence with the kernel source. pids_can_fork in kernel/cgroup/pids.c walks from the group to the root and charges each level, undoing the charges when a level is at its limit, as spawn does. Memory is charged in try_charge_memcg in mm/memcontrol.c, which climbs the hierarchy of struct page_counter, starts reclaim at the level that is over its limit, and calls mem_cgroup_out_of_memory when reclaim fails. The victim is chosen by oom_badness, which scores a process mainly by its memory use. The model omits reclaim.

The other controllers

The session of an ordinary user on this machine has only memory and pids. A container runtime that runs with privilege, or a service manager, also uses these.

ControllerMain fileEffect
cpucpu.max, for example 50000 100000The group may use 50 ms of CPU time in every period of 100 ms. A group that has used its quota is not scheduled until the next period.
cpucpu.weightA weight for the fair scheduler, applied to the group as a whole (chapter 6).
cpusetcpuset.cpusThe CPUs the tasks of the group may run on.
ioio.maxLimits on bytes and operations per second for a block device.
memorymemory.highA softer limit: above it, the group is slowed down and reclaimed, without the OOM killer.

cpu.max and memory.max are what the options --cpus and --memory of a container runtime set, and the resource limits of a Kubernetes pod are written to these files.

This chapter describes cgroup v2, in which all controllers share a single tree. The older cgroup v1 gave each controller a tree of its own, mounted separately, and it is still found on older systems. stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup prints cgroup2fs on a system that uses v2.

Inspecting control groups on a live system

CommandShows
cat /proc/<pid>/cgroupthe group of a process
cat <group>/cgroup.procsthe processes of a group
cat <group>/memory.current, pids.currentthe usage of a group and its descendants
cat <group>/memory.statthe memory of a group by kind
cat <group>/memory.events, pids.eventshow often a limit was hit, and how many processes were killed
systemd-cglsthe whole tree, with the processes in each group
systemd-cgtopthe groups ordered by their use of CPU and memory

A process that disappears without an error message has often been ended by the OOM killer of its group. memory.events of the group, and the kernel log shown by dmesg, record it.

The complete programs

Listing 12.23 The complete cgfacts, in Go. code/go/cgfacts/main.go

// Command cgfacts measures control groups. It creates a group below the one
// it runs in, starts shell commands inside the new group, and observes the
// kernel counting their processes, refusing a fork beyond pids.max, and
// ending a process that exceeds memory.max.
//
// Run it from code/go with:
//
//	go run ./cgfacts
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)


// A group is the directory of a control group under /sys/fs/cgroup.
type group string

// set writes a value to one of the group's control files.
func (g group) set(file, value string) error {
	return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(string(g), file), []byte(value), 0)
}

// get reads one of the group's control files.
func (g group) get(file string) (string, error) {
	text, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(string(g), file))

	return strings.TrimSpace(string(text)), err
}

// event returns the counter with the given key from a file of "key value"
// lines, such as pids.events and memory.events.
func (g group) event(file, key string) (string, error) {
	text, err := g.get(file)

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	for lines := bufio.NewScanner(strings.NewReader(text)); lines.Scan(); {
		if fields := strings.Fields(lines.Text()); len(fields) == 2 && fields[0] == key {
			return fields[1], nil
		}
	}

	return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: no line %q", file, key)
}


// create makes a new group. It goes up from the group of this process to the
// nearest group that distributes the memory and pids controllers to its
// children, and creates a directory there.
func create() (group, error) {
	line, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/self/cgroup")

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	_, path, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(line)), "::")

	for dir := filepath.Join("/sys/fs/cgroup", path); dir != "/sys/fs/cgroup"; dir = filepath.Dir(dir) {
		enabled, err := group(dir).get("cgroup.subtree_control")

		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(enabled, "memory") || !strings.Contains(enabled, "pids") {
			continue
		}

		created := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("cgfacts-%d", os.Getpid()))

		return group(created), os.Mkdir(created, 0o755)
	}

	return "", errors.New("no parent group delegates the memory and pids controllers")
}

// command returns a shell script that will run in the group. The shell
// first moves itself into the group by writing its own process number to
// cgroup.procs, and every process it starts afterwards is created there.
func (g group) command(script string) *exec.Cmd {
	return exec.Command("sh", "-c", `echo $$ > "$0/cgroup.procs" && `+script, string(g))
}

// remove ends every process left in the group, waits until the group is
// empty, and deletes it.
func (g group) remove() error {
	if err := g.set("cgroup.kill", "1"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	for {
		current, err := g.get("pids.current")

		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if current == "0" {
			return os.Remove(string(g))
		}

		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	}
}


// count starts a process in the group and reads the group's process count.
func count(g group) error {
	child := g.command("exec sleep 30")

	if err := child.Start(); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	current, err := g.get("pids.current")

	for err == nil && current != "1" {
		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
		current, err = g.get("pids.current")
	}

	child.Process.Kill()
	child.Wait()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	fmt.Printf("a process moved into the new group: pids.current %s\n", current)

	return nil
}


// limitPids sets pids.max to 4 and runs a shell that tries to start 6
// background commands and prints a line for each one it started.
func limitPids(g group) error {
	if err := g.set("pids.max", "4"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	started, _ := g.command("for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo started; done 2>/dev/null").Output()
	refused, err := g.event("pids.events", "max")

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	fmt.Printf("pids.max 4, a shell starts background commands: started %d, forks refused %s\n",
		strings.Count(string(started), "started"), refused)

	return g.set("pids.max", "max")
}


// limitMemory sets memory.max to 32 MiB with no swap and runs a command
// whose memory grows without bound.
func limitMemory(g group) error {
	if err := g.set("memory.max", "33554432"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := g.set("memory.swap.max", "0"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	child := g.command("exec tail /dev/zero")
	child.Run()

	kills, err := g.event("memory.events", "oom_kill")

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if status, ok := child.ProcessState.Sys().(syscall.WaitStatus); ok && status.Signaled() {
		fmt.Printf("memory.max 32 MiB, a command that grows without bound: killed by signal %d, oom_kill %s\n",
			status.Signal(), kills)
	}

	return nil
}


func run() error {
	g, err := create()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	for _, experiment := range []func(group) error{count, limitPids, limitMemory} {
		if err := experiment(g); err != nil {
			g.remove()

			return err
		}
	}

	return g.remove()
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

Listing 12.24 The complete cgfacts, in Rust. code/rust/cgfacts/src/main.rs

//! Measures control groups. It creates a group below the one it runs in,
//! starts shell commands inside the new group, and observes the kernel
//! counting their processes, refusing a fork beyond `pids.max`, and ending a
//! process that exceeds `memory.max`.
//!
//! Run it from code/rust with:
//!
//! ```text
//! cargo run -p cgfacts
//! ```

use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{self, Command};
use std::thread;
use std::time::Duration;

/// The directory of a control group under `/sys/fs/cgroup`.
struct Group(PathBuf);

impl Group {
    /// Writes a value to one of the group's control files.
    fn set(&self, file: &str, value: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
        fs::write(self.0.join(file), value)
    }

    /// Reads one of the group's control files.
    fn get(&self, file: &str) -> io::Result<String> {
        Ok(fs::read_to_string(self.0.join(file))?.trim().to_owned())
    }

    /// Returns the counter with the given key from a file of "key value"
    /// lines, such as `pids.events` and `memory.events`.
    fn event(&self, file: &str, key: &str) -> io::Result<String> {
        self.get(file)?
            .lines()
            .filter_map(|line| line.split_once(' '))
            .find(|(name, _)| *name == key)
            .map(|(_, value)| value.to_owned())
            .ok_or_else(|| io::ErrorKind::NotFound.into())
    }
}

impl Group {
    /// Makes a new group. It goes up from the group of this process to the
    /// nearest group that distributes the memory and pids controllers to its
    /// children, and creates a directory there.
    fn create() -> io::Result<Group> {
        let line = fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/cgroup")?;
        let path = line.trim().split_once("::").map_or("", |(_, path)| path);
        let root = Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup");
        let own = root.join(path.trim_start_matches('/'));

        for dir in own.ancestors().take_while(|dir| *dir != root) {
            let Ok(enabled) = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cgroup.subtree_control")) else {
                continue;
            };

            if enabled.contains("memory") && enabled.contains("pids") {
                let created = dir.join(format!("cgfacts-{}", process::id()));

                fs::create_dir(&created)?;

                return Ok(Group(created));
            }
        }

        Err(io::Error::other(
            "no parent group delegates the memory and pids controllers",
        ))
    }

    /// Returns a shell script that will run in the group. The shell first
    /// moves itself into the group by writing its own process number to
    /// `cgroup.procs`, and every process it starts afterwards is created
    /// there.
    fn command(&self, script: &str) -> Command {
        let mut command = Command::new("sh");

        command
            .arg("-c")
            .arg(format!(r#"echo $$ > "$0/cgroup.procs" && {script}"#))
            .arg(&self.0);

        command
    }

    /// Ends every process left in the group, waits until the group is empty,
    /// and deletes it.
    fn remove(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.set("cgroup.kill", "1")?;

        while self.get("pids.current")? != "0" {
            thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
        }

        fs::remove_dir(&self.0)
    }
}

/// Starts a process in the group and reads the group's process count.
fn count(group: &Group) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut child = group.command("exec sleep 30").spawn()?;

    while group.get("pids.current")? != "1" {
        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
    }

    child.kill()?;
    child.wait()?;

    println!("a process moved into the new group: pids.current 1");

    Ok(())
}

/// Sets `pids.max` to 4 and runs a shell that tries to start 6 background
/// commands and prints a line for each one it started.
fn limit_pids(group: &Group) -> io::Result<()> {
    group.set("pids.max", "4")?;

    let script = "for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo started; done 2>/dev/null";
    let output = group.command(script).output()?;
    let started = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout)
        .matches("started")
        .count();

    println!(
        "pids.max 4, a shell starts background commands: started {started}, forks refused {}",
        group.event("pids.events", "max")?
    );

    group.set("pids.max", "max")
}

/// Sets `memory.max` to 32 MiB with no swap and runs a command whose memory
/// grows without bound.
fn limit_memory(group: &Group) -> io::Result<()> {
    group.set("memory.max", "33554432")?;
    group.set("memory.swap.max", "0")?;

    let status = group.command("exec tail /dev/zero").status()?;
    let kills = group.event("memory.events", "oom_kill")?;

    if let Some(signal) = status.signal() {
        println!(
            "memory.max 32 MiB, a command that grows without bound: killed by signal {signal}, oom_kill {kills}"
        );
    }

    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let group = Group::create()?;

    let result = count(&group)
        .and_then(|()| limit_pids(&group))
        .and_then(|()| limit_memory(&group));

    group.remove()?;

    result
}

Listing 12.25 The complete cgmodel, in Go. code/go/cgmodel/main.go

// Command cgmodel models the control group hierarchy: every group counts the
// processes and the memory of its whole subtree, a fork is refused when any
// group above it is at its limit, and a group that exceeds its memory limit
// loses the largest process in its subtree.
//
// Run it from code/go with:
//
//	go run ./cgmodel
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math"
)


// unlimited is the value of a limit that is written "max" in a control file.
const unlimited = math.MaxInt

var errAgain = errors.New("EAGAIN")

// A group is one node of the hierarchy. pids and memory are the usage of the
// group and of every group below it. refused and oomKills are the counters
// the kernel publishes in pids.events and memory.events.
type group struct {
	name      string
	parent    *group
	children  []*group
	processes []*process

	pidsMax, memoryMax int
	pids, memory       int
	refused, oomKills  int
}

// A process belongs to one group and holds an amount of memory.
type process struct {
	name   string
	home   *group
	memory int
}

// child adds a group below g, with no limits of its own.
func (g *group) child(name string) *group {
	c := &group{name: name, parent: g, pidsMax: unlimited, memoryMax: unlimited}
	g.children = append(g.children, c)

	return c
}


// spawn starts a process in g. The process is counted in g and in every
// group above it, so it is refused when any of them is at its limit.
func (g *group) spawn(name string) (*process, error) {
	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		if up.pids == up.pidsMax {
			up.refused++

			return nil, errAgain
		}
	}

	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.pids++
	}

	p := &process{name: name, home: g}
	g.processes = append(g.processes, p)

	return p, nil
}


// charge adds an amount, which may be negative, to the memory count of a
// group and of every group above it.
func (g *group) charge(amount int) {
	for up := g; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.memory += amount
	}
}

// allocate gives a process more memory. While a group above the process is
// over its limit, the largest process in that group's subtree is killed. It
// returns the names of the processes killed.
func (p *process) allocate(amount int) []string {
	p.memory += amount
	p.home.charge(amount)

	var killed []string

	for up := p.home; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		for up.memory > up.memoryMax {
			victim := up.largest()
			up.oomKills++
			killed = append(killed, victim.name)
			victim.kill()
		}
	}

	return killed
}

// largest returns the process with the most memory in the subtree of g.
func (g *group) largest() *process {
	var found *process

	for _, p := range g.processes {
		if found == nil || p.memory > found.memory {
			found = p
		}
	}

	for _, c := range g.children {
		if p := c.largest(); p != nil && (found == nil || p.memory > found.memory) {
			found = p
		}
	}

	return found
}

// kill removes a process from its group and returns its memory and its
// place in the process count.
func (p *process) kill() {
	p.home.charge(-p.memory)

	for up := p.home; up != nil; up = up.parent {
		up.pids--
	}

	for i, other := range p.home.processes {
		if other == p {
			p.home.processes = append(p.home.processes[:i], p.home.processes[i+1:]...)

			break
		}
	}
}


func main() {
	team := &group{name: "team", pidsMax: 4, memoryMax: 100}
	jobA, jobB := team.child("job-a"), team.child("job-b")

	var started []*process

	for _, start := range []struct {
		in   *group
		name string
	}{{jobA, "a1"}, {jobA, "a2"}, {jobA, "a3"}, {jobB, "b1"}} {
		p, err := start.in.spawn(start.name)

		if err != nil {
			fmt.Println(err)

			return
		}

		started = append(started, p)
	}

	fmt.Printf("3 processes in job-a and 1 in job-b: pids.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d\n",
		jobA.pids, jobB.pids, team.pids)

	_, err := jobB.spawn("b2")
	fmt.Printf("another process in job-b, team at pids.max 4: %v, pids.events max of team %d\n", err, team.refused)

	a1, b1 := started[0], started[3]

	a1.allocate(60)
	fmt.Printf("a1 allocates 60: memory.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d\n", jobA.memory, jobB.memory, team.memory)

	killed := b1.allocate(50)
	fmt.Printf("b1 allocates 50, team at memory.max 100: killed %v, oom_kill of team %d\n", killed, team.oomKills)
	fmt.Printf("afterwards: memory.current job-a %d, job-b %d, team %d, pids.current team %d\n",
		jobA.memory, jobB.memory, team.memory, team.pids)
}

Listing 12.26 The complete cgmodel, in Rust. code/rust/cgmodel/src/main.rs

//! Models the control group hierarchy: every group counts the processes and
//! the memory of its whole subtree, a fork is refused when any group above
//! it is at its limit, and a group that exceeds its memory limit loses the
//! largest process in its subtree.
//!
//! Run it from code/rust with:
//!
//! ```text
//! cargo run -p cgmodel
//! ```

use std::fmt;

/// The value of a limit that is written "max" in a control file.
const UNLIMITED: usize = usize::MAX;

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Again;

impl fmt::Display for Again {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("EAGAIN")
    }
}

/// One node of the hierarchy. `pids` and `memory` are the usage of the group
/// and of every group below it. `refused` and `oom_kills` are the counters
/// the kernel publishes in `pids.events` and `memory.events`.
struct Group {
    parent: Option<usize>,
    pids_max: usize,
    memory_max: usize,
    pids: usize,
    memory: usize,
    refused: usize,
    oom_kills: usize,
}

/// A process belongs to one group and holds an amount of memory.
struct Process {
    name: &'static str,
    home: usize,
    memory: usize,
    alive: bool,
}

/// The hierarchy: groups and processes, referred to by index.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Hierarchy {
    groups: Vec<Group>,
    processes: Vec<Process>,
}

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Adds a group below `parent` and returns its index.
    fn group(&mut self, parent: Option<usize>, pids_max: usize, memory_max: usize) -> usize {
        self.groups.push(Group {
            parent,
            pids_max,
            memory_max,
            pids: 0,
            memory: 0,
            refused: 0,
            oom_kills: 0,
        });

        self.groups.len() - 1
    }

    /// The group itself and every group above it, nearest first.
    fn upward(&self, group: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
        let mut path = vec![group];

        while let Some(parent) = self.groups[path[path.len() - 1]].parent {
            path.push(parent);
        }

        path
    }
}

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Starts a process in a group and returns its index. The process is
    /// counted in the group and in every group above it, so it is refused
    /// when any of them is at its limit.
    fn spawn(&mut self, group: usize, name: &'static str) -> Result<usize, Again> {
        let path = self.upward(group);

        for &up in &path {
            if self.groups[up].pids == self.groups[up].pids_max {
                self.groups[up].refused += 1;

                return Err(Again);
            }
        }

        for &up in &path {
            self.groups[up].pids += 1;
        }

        self.processes.push(Process {
            name,
            home: group,
            memory: 0,
            alive: true,
        });

        Ok(self.processes.len() - 1)
    }
}

impl Hierarchy {
    /// Gives a process more memory. While a group above the process is over
    /// its limit, the largest process in that group's subtree is killed.
    /// Returns the names of the processes killed.
    fn allocate(&mut self, process: usize, amount: usize) -> Vec<&'static str> {
        let path = self.upward(self.processes[process].home);

        self.processes[process].memory += amount;

        for &up in &path {
            self.groups[up].memory += amount;
        }

        let mut killed = Vec::new();

        for &up in &path {
            while self.groups[up].memory > self.groups[up].memory_max {
                let Some(victim) = self.largest(up) else {
                    break;
                };

                self.groups[up].oom_kills += 1;
                killed.push(self.processes[victim].name);
                self.kill(victim);
            }
        }

        killed
    }

    /// Returns the living process with the most memory in the subtree of a
    /// group.
    fn largest(&self, group: usize) -> Option<usize> {
        (0..self.processes.len())
            .filter(|&p| self.processes[p].alive)
            .filter(|&p| self.upward(self.processes[p].home).contains(&group))
            .max_by_key(|&p| self.processes[p].memory)
    }

    /// Ends a process and returns its memory and its place in the process
    /// count.
    fn kill(&mut self, process: usize) {
        let memory = self.processes[process].memory;

        for up in self.upward(self.processes[process].home) {
            self.groups[up].memory -= memory;
            self.groups[up].pids -= 1;
        }

        self.processes[process].alive = false;
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Again> {
    let mut tree = Hierarchy::default();

    let team = tree.group(None, 4, 100);
    let job_a = tree.group(Some(team), UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED);
    let job_b = tree.group(Some(team), UNLIMITED, UNLIMITED);

    let a1 = tree.spawn(job_a, "a1")?;
    tree.spawn(job_a, "a2")?;
    tree.spawn(job_a, "a3")?;
    let b1 = tree.spawn(job_b, "b1")?;

    println!(
        "3 processes in job-a and 1 in job-b: pids.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].pids, tree.groups[job_b].pids, tree.groups[team].pids
    );

    if let Err(error) = tree.spawn(job_b, "b2") {
        println!(
            "another process in job-b, team at pids.max 4: {error}, pids.events max of team {}",
            tree.groups[team].refused
        );
    }

    tree.allocate(a1, 60);
    println!(
        "a1 allocates 60: memory.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].memory, tree.groups[job_b].memory, tree.groups[team].memory
    );

    let killed = tree.allocate(b1, 50);
    println!(
        "b1 allocates 50, team at memory.max 100: killed [{}], oom_kill of team {}",
        killed.join(" "),
        tree.groups[team].oom_kills
    );
    println!(
        "afterwards: memory.current job-a {}, job-b {}, team {}, pids.current team {}",
        tree.groups[job_a].memory,
        tree.groups[job_b].memory,
        tree.groups[team].memory,
        tree.groups[team].pids
    );

    Ok(())
}

Summary

  • A control group is a set of processes with shared accounting and limits. Groups are directories under /sys/fs/cgroup, and their settings are files.
  • Writing a pid to cgroup.procs moves a process into a group. Its children start in the same group.
  • A group has the files of a controller only if its parent passes that controller on in cgroup.subtree_control.
  • At pids.max, a fork in the group fails with EAGAIN.
  • At memory.max, the kernel reclaims memory from the group, and when that fails it ends a process in the group with SIGKILL.
  • The counters and limits of a group cover its whole subtree.

References

  • cgroups(7), Linux manual page: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/cgroups.7.html
  • Control Group v2, Linux kernel documentation: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v5.15/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html
  • kernel/cgroup/pids.c and mm/memcontrol.c, Linux 5.15: https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.15/source/kernel/cgroup/pids.c

Building a Container

A container is an ordinary process that runs with a restricted view of the system and with limits on what it may use. The kernel has no object called a container. A container runtime builds one from the mechanisms of the previous chapters: namespaces for the view, a root file system for the files, and a control group for the limits.

In this chapter, we will write box, a program that starts a shell in a container. It needs no privileges and no container software. We will build it in stages: the control group, the creation of the first process in new namespaces, the root file system, and the final exec.

This chapter covers

  • the parts of a container and the kernel mechanism behind each
  • starting a process directly inside a control group
  • assembling a root file system from a tmpfs and bind mounts
  • pivot_root: replacing the root directory of a mount namespace
  • why /proc has to be mounted again inside the container
  • what happens to the other processes of a container when its first process ends
  • what the container sees: its mounts, its network, its capabilities
  • what a container image is, and how docker run reaches the calls of this chapter

The parts

PartMechanismCovered in
its own process numbersPID namespacechapter 11
its own host nameUTS namespacechapter 11
user 0 inside, an ordinary user outsideuser namespacechapter 11
its own mounted file systemsmount namespacethis chapter
its own network interfacesnetwork namespacechapter 11
its own root directorypivot_rootthis chapter
limits on processes and memorycontrol groupchapter 12
a first process that runs a programclone and execchapter 3

A mount namespace holds the list of mounted file systems that its processes see. A process in a new mount namespace starts with a copy of its parent’s list and can then mount and unmount without any effect outside. box uses that freedom to assemble a directory tree for the container and to make it the root.

A real container image supplies a complete root file system, with its own programs and libraries. box has no image. It borrows the program directories of the host, which keeps the example self-contained, and exposes nothing else: the home directories, /etc and /tmp of the host do not exist inside.

Mounts and the root directory

A mount attaches a file system at a directory, the mount point. The files of the file system then appear below that directory. What a process sees at / is the mount at the top of its mount namespace, and a path such as /usr/bin/ls is resolved by walking down from there, crossing into another file system at each mount point.

box needs 3 kinds of mount, all made with the mount system call.

KindCallEffect
a new file systemmount("tmpfs", dir, "tmpfs", ...)an empty file system held in memory appears at dir
a bind mountmount("/usr", dir, NULL, MS_BIND, ...)the existing directory /usr also appears at dir; the files are the same files
a change of propagationmount(NULL, "/", NULL, MS_REC | MS_PRIVATE, ...)mounts made from now on are not copied to other mount namespaces

The root directory is changed with pivot_root, in 3 steps.

An older call, chroot, also changes what a process sees as /. It changes only the starting point of path lookup and leaves the host’s file system mounted, and a process with privilege can get out of it. pivot_root followed by the unmount removes the host’s tree from the mount namespace altogether, which is why container runtimes use it.

Setting up

box uses golang.org/x/sys/unix in Go and the nix crate with 5 features in Rust.

$ cargo new box
$ cargo add -p box nix --features fs,hostname,mount,sched,user

Low-level design: box

FunctionRuns inBehaviour
createGroup(pidsMax)the parentcreates a control group and sets its limit
launch(group, root, script)the parentstarts the first process of the container in new namespaces and in the group
buildRoot(root)process 1mounts a tmpfs on root and populates it
enterRoot(root)process 1makes root the root directory and detaches the host’s tree
initialize(root, script)process 1builds and enters the root, sets the host name, executes the shell

The control group

createGroup is the code of chapter 12: it finds the nearest group that passes on the pids controller and creates a directory below it. The group is created before the container, so that the first process of the container can start inside it.

use std::process::{self, Command};

Listing 13.3 Creating the control group of the container, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// createGroup makes a control group for the container below the nearest
// group that passes the pids controller to its children, and sets pids.max.
func createGroup(pidsMax int) (string, error) {
	line, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/self/cgroup")

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	_, path, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(line)), "::")

	for dir := filepath.Join("/sys/fs/cgroup", path); dir != "/sys/fs/cgroup"; dir = filepath.Dir(dir) {
		enabled, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cgroup.subtree_control"))

		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(string(enabled), "pids") {
			continue
		}

		group := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("box-%d", os.Getpid()))

		if err := os.Mkdir(group, 0o755); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}

		return group, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(group, "pids.max"), fmt.Append(nil, pidsMax), 0)
	}

	return "", errors.New("no parent group passes on the pids controller")
}

// refused returns the number of forks the group has refused.
func refused(group string) (string, error) {
	events, err := os.Open(filepath.Join(group, "pids.events"))

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	defer events.Close()

	for lines := bufio.NewScanner(events); lines.Scan(); {
		if count, ok := strings.CutPrefix(lines.Text(), "max "); ok {
			return count, nil
		}
	}

	return "", errors.New("pids.events has no line max")
}

// removeGroup waits until the group is empty and deletes it.
func removeGroup(group string) error {
	for {
		current, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(group, "pids.current"))

		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if strings.TrimSpace(string(current)) == "0" {
			return os.Remove(group)
		}

		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	}
}

Listing 13.4 Creating the control group of the container, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

/// Makes a control group for the container below the nearest group that
/// passes the pids controller to its children, and sets `pids.max`.
fn create_group(pids_max: u32) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
    let line = fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/cgroup")?;
    let path = line.trim().split_once("::").map_or("", |(_, path)| path);

    let root = Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup");
    let own = root.join(path.trim_start_matches('/'));

    for dir in own.ancestors().take_while(|dir| *dir != root) {
        let Ok(enabled) = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cgroup.subtree_control")) else {
            continue;
        };

        if enabled.contains("pids") {
            let group = dir.join(format!("box-{}", process::id()));

            fs::create_dir(&group)?;
            fs::write(group.join("pids.max"), pids_max.to_string())?;

            return Ok(group);
        }
    }

    Err(io::Error::other(
        "no parent group passes on the pids controller",
    ))
}

/// Returns the number of forks the group has refused.
fn refused(group: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
    fs::read_to_string(group.join("pids.events"))?
        .lines()
        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("max "))
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("pids.events has no line max"))
}

/// Waits until the group is empty and deletes it.
fn remove_group(group: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    while fs::read_to_string(group.join("pids.current"))?.trim() != "0" {
        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
    }

    fs::remove_dir(group)
}

The first process

box starts itself again with the argument init, in new user, mount, UTS, PID, IPC and network namespaces. As in chapter 11, the languages differ in how the namespaces are created.

The Go version passes everything to the call that creates the child. Cloneflags names the namespaces, the mappings make the current user user 0 inside, and CgroupFD asks the kernel to create the child directly in the control group, so there is no interval in which the child runs outside it.

The Rust version starts a helper process that calls unshare and writes the mappings, and the helper starts the first process. That process then moves itself into the group by writing 0, which stands for the writing process, to cgroup.procs.

Listing 13.5 Starting the first process of the container, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// launch starts this program again as the first process of a container. The
// clone flags create the namespaces, the mappings make the current user
// user 0 inside, and CgroupFD makes the kernel create the child inside the
// control group.
func launch(group, root, script string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
	directory, err := os.Open(group)

	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	defer directory.Close()

	child := exec.Command("/proc/self/exe", "init", root, script)
	child.Stdout, child.Stderr = os.Stdout, os.Stderr

	child.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
		Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWUSER | syscall.CLONE_NEWNS | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS |
			syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWIPC | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET,
		UidMappings: []syscall.SysProcIDMap{{ContainerID: 0, HostID: os.Getuid(), Size: 1}},
		GidMappings: []syscall.SysProcIDMap{{ContainerID: 0, HostID: os.Getgid(), Size: 1}},
		UseCgroupFD: true,
		CgroupFD:    int(directory.Fd()),
	}

	return child, child.Start()
}

Listing 13.6 Starting the first process of the container, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

/// Runs in a helper process. It moves itself into new namespaces, maps the
/// current user to user 0 inside, and starts the first process of the
/// container. The new PID namespace takes effect for that child.
fn enter(group: &str, root: &str, script: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    let (uid, gid) = (getuid(), getgid());

    unshare(
        CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWUSER
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWNS
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWUTS
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWPID
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWIPC
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWNET,
    )?;

    fs::write("/proc/self/setgroups", "deny")?;
    fs::write("/proc/self/uid_map", format!("0 {uid} 1"))?;
    fs::write("/proc/self/gid_map", format!("0 {gid} 1"))?;

    let status = Command::new("/proc/self/exe")
        .args(["init", group, root, script])
        .status()?;

    let Some(code) = status.code() else {
        process::exit(1);
    };

    process::exit(code);
}

The root file system

buildRoot runs inside the new mount namespace. Its first call sets the propagation of every mount to private. Without it, mounts made here could be copied back to the host’s namespace, depending on how the host is configured.

It then mounts a tmpfs, a file system held in memory, on an empty directory. This is the future root. It makes the host’s program directories visible below it with bind mounts: a bind mount shows an existing directory at a second place. The container also receives the device /dev/null, which shell scripts expect.

The last mount is a new /proc. The /proc of the host describes the host’s PID namespace. A proc file system mounted from inside the new PID namespace describes that namespace, and shows the container only its own processes.

enterRoot calls pivot_root, which makes the new directory the root of the mount namespace and attaches the previous root at a directory inside it. Unmounting that directory removes the last path from the container to the host’s files.

Listing 13.7 Building the root file system, and entering it, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// shared are the directories of the host that the container can see.
var shared = []string{"bin", "sbin", "lib", "usr"}

// buildRoot assembles the root file system of the container in an empty
// directory: a tmpfs, the host's program directories, the null device, and
// a new /proc.
func buildRoot(root string) error {
	// Mount changes made from here on stay in this mount namespace.
	if err := unix.Mount("", "/", "", unix.MS_REC|unix.MS_PRIVATE, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("make mounts private: %w", err)
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("tmpfs", root, "tmpfs", 0, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mount tmpfs: %w", err)
	}

	for _, name := range shared {
		source, target := "/"+name, filepath.Join(root, name)

		// On this system /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links into /usr.
		if link, err := os.Readlink(source); err == nil {
			if err := os.Symlink(link, target); err != nil {
				return err
			}

			continue
		}

		if err := os.Mkdir(target, 0o755); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := unix.Mount(source, target, "", unix.MS_BIND|unix.MS_REC, ""); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bind %s: %w", source, err)
		}
	}

	// The container gets a /dev with the null device and nothing else.
	null := filepath.Join(root, "dev", "null")

	if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Dir(null), 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(null, nil, 0o666); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("/dev/null", null, "", unix.MS_BIND, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("bind /dev/null: %w", err)
	}

	proc := filepath.Join(root, "proc")

	if err := os.Mkdir(proc, 0o555); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("proc", proc, "proc", 0, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mount proc: %w", err)
	}

	return nil
}

// enterRoot makes root the root directory of the mount namespace and
// detaches the host's file system from it.
func enterRoot(root string) error {
	old := filepath.Join(root, "old")

	if err := os.Mkdir(old, 0o700); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.PivotRoot(root, old); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("pivot_root: %w", err)
	}

	if err := os.Chdir("/"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Unmount("/old", unix.MNT_DETACH); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("unmount the old root: %w", err)
	}

	return os.Remove("/old")
}

Listing 13.8 Building the root file system, and entering it, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

/// The directories of the host that the container can see.
const SHARED: [&str; 4] = ["bin", "sbin", "lib", "usr"];

/// No source, file system type or options, for the calls to `mount` that
/// need none.
const NONE: Option<&str> = None;

/// Assembles the root file system of the container in an empty directory: a
/// tmpfs, the host's program directories, the null device, and a new /proc.
fn build_root(root: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    // Mount changes made from here on stay in this mount namespace.
    mount(NONE, "/", NONE, MsFlags::MS_REC | MsFlags::MS_PRIVATE, NONE)?;
    mount(Some("tmpfs"), root, Some("tmpfs"), MsFlags::empty(), NONE)?;

    for name in SHARED {
        let (source, target) = (Path::new("/").join(name), root.join(name));

        // On this system /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links into /usr.
        if let Ok(link) = fs::read_link(&source) {
            symlink(link, target)?;

            continue;
        }

        fs::create_dir(&target)?;
        mount(
            Some(&source),
            &target,
            NONE,
            MsFlags::MS_BIND | MsFlags::MS_REC,
            NONE,
        )?;
    }

    // The container gets a /dev with the null device and nothing else.
    let null = root.join("dev/null");

    fs::create_dir(root.join("dev"))?;
    fs::write(&null, "")?;
    mount(Some("/dev/null"), &null, NONE, MsFlags::MS_BIND, NONE)?;

    let proc = root.join("proc");

    fs::create_dir(&proc)?;
    mount(Some("proc"), &proc, Some("proc"), MsFlags::empty(), NONE)?;

    Ok(())
}

/// Makes `root` the root directory of the mount namespace and detaches the
/// host's file system from it.
fn enter_root(root: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    let old = root.join("old");

    fs::create_dir(&old)?;
    pivot_root(root, &old)?;
    chdir("/")?;
    umount2("/old", MntFlags::MNT_DETACH)?;

    fs::remove_dir("/old")
}

Becoming the program

initialize runs the steps in order and ends with exec. The process that set up the container is replaced by the shell, which is therefore process 1 of the container.

Listing 13.9 The first process: set up, then exec, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// initialize runs as process 1 of the container. It builds and enters the
// root file system, sets the host name, and replaces itself with a shell
// that runs the script.
func initialize(root, script string) error {
	if err := buildRoot(root); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := enterRoot(root); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Sethostname([]byte("box")); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	environment := []string{"PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"}

	return unix.Exec("/bin/sh", []string{"sh", "-c", script}, environment)
}

Listing 13.10 The first process: set up, then exec, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

/// Runs as process 1 of the container. It moves itself into the control
/// group, where writing 0 to `cgroup.procs` means "the writing process".
/// Then it builds and enters the root file system, sets the host name, and
/// replaces itself with a shell that runs the script.
fn initialize(group: &Path, root: &Path, script: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    fs::write(group.join("cgroup.procs"), "0")?;

    build_root(root)?;
    enter_root(root)?;
    sethostname("box")?;

    let error = Command::new("/bin/sh")
        .args(["-c", script])
        .env_clear()
        .env("PATH", "/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin")
        .exec();

    Err(error)
}

run is the parent’s side. The script reports what the shell sees and then tries to start 6 background commands under a pids.max of 5.

Listing 13.11 Running the container, and reporting on it, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// script is what the container runs.
const script = `echo "host name: $(hostname)"
echo "process number of the shell: $$"
echo "user number: $(id -u)"
echo "processes under /proc:" /proc/[0-9]*
echo "root directory:" /*
while read device directory type rest; do echo "mounted: $directory ($type)"; done < /proc/mounts
echo "network interfaces:" $(tail -n +3 /proc/net/dev | cut -d: -f1)
echo "effective capabilities:" $(grep CapEff /proc/self/status | cut -f2)
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo "started a background command"; done 2>/dev/null`

func run() error {
	group, err := createGroup(5)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	defer removeGroup(group)

	root, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "box-root")

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	defer os.Remove(root)

	before, err := os.Hostname()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	child, err := launch(group, root, script)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	child.Wait()

	count, err := refused(group)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	after, err := os.Hostname()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	fmt.Printf("the container ended with status %d; forks refused by its group: %s\n", child.ProcessState.ExitCode(), count)
	fmt.Printf("host name outside unchanged: %v\n", before == after)

	return nil
}

func main() {
	var err error

	if len(os.Args) == 4 && os.Args[1] == "init" {
		err = initialize(os.Args[2], os.Args[3])
	} else {
		err = run()
	}

	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

Listing 13.12 Running the container, and reporting on it, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

/// What the container runs.
const SCRIPT: &str = r#"echo "host name: $(hostname)"
echo "process number of the shell: $$"
echo "user number: $(id -u)"
echo "processes under /proc:" /proc/[0-9]*
echo "root directory:" /*
while read device directory type rest; do echo "mounted: $directory ($type)"; done < /proc/mounts
echo "network interfaces:" $(tail -n +3 /proc/net/dev | cut -d: -f1)
echo "effective capabilities:" $(grep CapEff /proc/self/status | cut -f2)
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo "started a background command"; done 2>/dev/null"#;

fn hostname() -> io::Result<String> {
    Ok(gethostname()?.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
}

fn run() -> io::Result<()> {
    let group = create_group(5)?;
    let root = env::temp_dir().join(format!("box-root-{}", process::id()));

    fs::create_dir(&root)?;

    let before = hostname()?;

    let status = Command::new("/proc/self/exe")
        .arg("enter")
        .args([&group, &root])
        .arg(SCRIPT)
        .status()?;

    let Some(code) = status.code() else {
        return Err(io::Error::other("the container was ended by a signal"));
    };

    let count = refused(&group)?;

    remove_group(&group)?;
    fs::remove_dir(&root)?;

    println!("the container ended with status {code}; forks refused by its group: {count}");
    println!("host name outside unchanged: {}", before == hostname()?);

    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    let args: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();

    match args.as_slice() {
        [_, "enter", group, root, script] => enter(group, root, script),
        [_, "init", group, root, script] => initialize(Path::new(group), Path::new(root), script),
        _ => run(),
    }
}

process number of the shell: 1
user number: 0
processes under /proc: /proc/1
root directory: /bin /dev /lib /proc /sbin /usr
mounted: / (tmpfs)
mounted: /usr (ext4)
mounted: /dev/null (devtmpfs)
mounted: /proc (proc)

OutputWhat it shows
host name box, unchanged outsideThe UTS namespace contains the change.
process number 1The shell is the first process of the PID namespace.
user number 0The user namespace maps the invoking user to user 0.
/proc/1 onlyThe new /proc shows the container’s processes. The glob is expanded by the shell itself, so no second process exists at that moment.
/bin /dev /lib /proc /sbin /usrThe root directory is the tmpfs that buildRoot assembled.
mounted: 4 linesThe mount namespace contains exactly what buildRoot made: the tmpfs at /, the host’s /usr, the null device, and the new /proc. The disks, /home and /tmp of the host are absent.
network interfaces: loA new network namespace has only a loopback interface. The container cannot reach the network, and the host’s interfaces are invisible.
effective capabilities 000001ffffffffffEvery capability bit is set. They apply inside the user namespace only (chapter 11).
4 commands started, 1 fork refusedThe shell and 4 commands reach pids.max 5, and the next fork fails.
status 2The shell stops at the failed fork and exits with an error status.

The table states the central fact about containers. A container is a view. The process inside is an ordinary process of the host, scheduled by the same scheduler and using the same memory, and the kernel answers its questions from a restricted set of objects.

When the shell exits, 4 sleep commands are still running. The shell was process 1 of its PID namespace, and when the first process of a PID namespace ends, the kernel ends every other process in it. No process of the container survives its first process, which is why box can remove the control group as soon as its count reaches 0.

What a production runtime adds. box leaves out several parts of a container runtime such as runc. It has no image and shares the host’s programs. Its network namespace has only a loopback interface, where a runtime creates a pair of virtual Ethernet devices and moves one end into the container to connect it. It keeps all capabilities inside its user namespace and installs no system call filter, where a runtime drops most capabilities and applies a seccomp filter, a list of permitted system calls, to reduce what a compromised program can ask of the kernel. And it sets a single limit, where a runtime sets memory, CPU and I/O limits as well.

A container is an ordinary process. ps, /proc and every other tool of the earlier chapters work on it from the host.

Images and runtimes

box borrows /usr from the host. A real container brings its own files, as an image: an archive of a root file system, built in layers.

The layers are combined by an overlay file system, overlayfs. It is mounted with a list of read-only directories, the lower layers, and a single writable directory, the upper layer, and it shows their union. A file is looked up in the upper layer first and then in each lower layer. A write to a file from a lower layer first copies the file to the upper layer. The image is not modified, so many containers share its layers, and each container’s changes are confined to its own upper layer. In terms of this chapter, a runtime replaces the tmpfs and the bind mounts of buildRoot with a single overlay mount, and everything after that is the same.

The software that people call “Docker” is several programs in a chain, and only the last makes the system calls.

The interface between the engine and the runtime is standardised by the Open Container Initiative. The engine unpacks the image and writes a file, config.json, that lists the namespaces to create, the mounts to make, the limits to set, and the command to run. The runtime carries it out. box is a runtime with its configuration fixed in the source.

Inspecting a container

A container is a set of ordinary processes, so every tool of the earlier chapters applies to it from the host.

CommandShows
ps -ef --forestthe processes of a container, as children of its runtime, with their pids on the host
ls -l /proc/<pid>/nsthe namespaces of a container process (chapter 11)
cat /proc/<pid>/cgroupits control group (chapter 12)
cat /proc/<pid>/mountinfothe mounts of its mount namespace
cat /proc/<pid>/uid_mapthe user mapping, when it runs in a user namespace
nsenter --target <pid> --all sha shell inside all namespaces of the container

The complete program

Listing 13.13 The complete box, in Go. code/go/box/main.go

// Command box runs a shell script in a container built by hand: new user,
// mount, UTS, PID, IPC and network namespaces, a root file system of its own, and a
// control group with a limit on the number of processes.
//
// Run it from code/go with:
//
//	go run ./box
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
)


// createGroup makes a control group for the container below the nearest
// group that passes the pids controller to its children, and sets pids.max.
func createGroup(pidsMax int) (string, error) {
	line, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/self/cgroup")

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	_, path, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(line)), "::")

	for dir := filepath.Join("/sys/fs/cgroup", path); dir != "/sys/fs/cgroup"; dir = filepath.Dir(dir) {
		enabled, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cgroup.subtree_control"))

		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(string(enabled), "pids") {
			continue
		}

		group := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("box-%d", os.Getpid()))

		if err := os.Mkdir(group, 0o755); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}

		return group, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(group, "pids.max"), fmt.Append(nil, pidsMax), 0)
	}

	return "", errors.New("no parent group passes on the pids controller")
}

// refused returns the number of forks the group has refused.
func refused(group string) (string, error) {
	events, err := os.Open(filepath.Join(group, "pids.events"))

	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}

	defer events.Close()

	for lines := bufio.NewScanner(events); lines.Scan(); {
		if count, ok := strings.CutPrefix(lines.Text(), "max "); ok {
			return count, nil
		}
	}

	return "", errors.New("pids.events has no line max")
}

// removeGroup waits until the group is empty and deletes it.
func removeGroup(group string) error {
	for {
		current, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(group, "pids.current"))

		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if strings.TrimSpace(string(current)) == "0" {
			return os.Remove(group)
		}

		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	}
}


// launch starts this program again as the first process of a container. The
// clone flags create the namespaces, the mappings make the current user
// user 0 inside, and CgroupFD makes the kernel create the child inside the
// control group.
func launch(group, root, script string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
	directory, err := os.Open(group)

	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	defer directory.Close()

	child := exec.Command("/proc/self/exe", "init", root, script)
	child.Stdout, child.Stderr = os.Stdout, os.Stderr

	child.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
		Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWUSER | syscall.CLONE_NEWNS | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS |
			syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWIPC | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET,
		UidMappings: []syscall.SysProcIDMap{{ContainerID: 0, HostID: os.Getuid(), Size: 1}},
		GidMappings: []syscall.SysProcIDMap{{ContainerID: 0, HostID: os.Getgid(), Size: 1}},
		UseCgroupFD: true,
		CgroupFD:    int(directory.Fd()),
	}

	return child, child.Start()
}


// shared are the directories of the host that the container can see.
var shared = []string{"bin", "sbin", "lib", "usr"}

// buildRoot assembles the root file system of the container in an empty
// directory: a tmpfs, the host's program directories, the null device, and
// a new /proc.
func buildRoot(root string) error {
	// Mount changes made from here on stay in this mount namespace.
	if err := unix.Mount("", "/", "", unix.MS_REC|unix.MS_PRIVATE, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("make mounts private: %w", err)
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("tmpfs", root, "tmpfs", 0, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mount tmpfs: %w", err)
	}

	for _, name := range shared {
		source, target := "/"+name, filepath.Join(root, name)

		// On this system /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links into /usr.
		if link, err := os.Readlink(source); err == nil {
			if err := os.Symlink(link, target); err != nil {
				return err
			}

			continue
		}

		if err := os.Mkdir(target, 0o755); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		if err := unix.Mount(source, target, "", unix.MS_BIND|unix.MS_REC, ""); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bind %s: %w", source, err)
		}
	}

	// The container gets a /dev with the null device and nothing else.
	null := filepath.Join(root, "dev", "null")

	if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Dir(null), 0o755); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := os.WriteFile(null, nil, 0o666); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("/dev/null", null, "", unix.MS_BIND, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("bind /dev/null: %w", err)
	}

	proc := filepath.Join(root, "proc")

	if err := os.Mkdir(proc, 0o555); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Mount("proc", proc, "proc", 0, ""); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mount proc: %w", err)
	}

	return nil
}

// enterRoot makes root the root directory of the mount namespace and
// detaches the host's file system from it.
func enterRoot(root string) error {
	old := filepath.Join(root, "old")

	if err := os.Mkdir(old, 0o700); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.PivotRoot(root, old); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("pivot_root: %w", err)
	}

	if err := os.Chdir("/"); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Unmount("/old", unix.MNT_DETACH); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("unmount the old root: %w", err)
	}

	return os.Remove("/old")
}


// initialize runs as process 1 of the container. It builds and enters the
// root file system, sets the host name, and replaces itself with a shell
// that runs the script.
func initialize(root, script string) error {
	if err := buildRoot(root); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := enterRoot(root); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err := unix.Sethostname([]byte("box")); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	environment := []string{"PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"}

	return unix.Exec("/bin/sh", []string{"sh", "-c", script}, environment)
}


// script is what the container runs.
const script = `echo "host name: $(hostname)"
echo "process number of the shell: $$"
echo "user number: $(id -u)"
echo "processes under /proc:" /proc/[0-9]*
echo "root directory:" /*
while read device directory type rest; do echo "mounted: $directory ($type)"; done < /proc/mounts
echo "network interfaces:" $(tail -n +3 /proc/net/dev | cut -d: -f1)
echo "effective capabilities:" $(grep CapEff /proc/self/status | cut -f2)
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo "started a background command"; done 2>/dev/null`

func run() error {
	group, err := createGroup(5)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	defer removeGroup(group)

	root, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "box-root")

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	defer os.Remove(root)

	before, err := os.Hostname()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	child, err := launch(group, root, script)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	child.Wait()

	count, err := refused(group)

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	after, err := os.Hostname()

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	fmt.Printf("the container ended with status %d; forks refused by its group: %s\n", child.ProcessState.ExitCode(), count)
	fmt.Printf("host name outside unchanged: %v\n", before == after)

	return nil
}

func main() {
	var err error

	if len(os.Args) == 4 && os.Args[1] == "init" {
		err = initialize(os.Args[2], os.Args[3])
	} else {
		err = run()
	}

	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

Listing 13.14 The complete box, in Rust. code/rust/box/src/main.rs

//! Runs a shell script in a container built by hand: new user, mount, UTS,
//! PID, IPC and network namespaces, a root file system of its own, and a control group
//! with a limit on the number of processes.
//!
//! Run it from code/rust with:
//!
//! ```text
//! cargo run -p box
//! ```

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;
use std::os::unix::process::CommandExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{self, Command};
use std::thread;
use std::time::Duration;

use nix::mount::{MntFlags, MsFlags, mount, umount2};
use nix::sched::{CloneFlags, unshare};
use nix::unistd::{chdir, getgid, gethostname, getuid, pivot_root, sethostname};

/// Makes a control group for the container below the nearest group that
/// passes the pids controller to its children, and sets `pids.max`.
fn create_group(pids_max: u32) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
    let line = fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/cgroup")?;
    let path = line.trim().split_once("::").map_or("", |(_, path)| path);

    let root = Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup");
    let own = root.join(path.trim_start_matches('/'));

    for dir in own.ancestors().take_while(|dir| *dir != root) {
        let Ok(enabled) = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cgroup.subtree_control")) else {
            continue;
        };

        if enabled.contains("pids") {
            let group = dir.join(format!("box-{}", process::id()));

            fs::create_dir(&group)?;
            fs::write(group.join("pids.max"), pids_max.to_string())?;

            return Ok(group);
        }
    }

    Err(io::Error::other(
        "no parent group passes on the pids controller",
    ))
}

/// Returns the number of forks the group has refused.
fn refused(group: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
    fs::read_to_string(group.join("pids.events"))?
        .lines()
        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("max "))
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("pids.events has no line max"))
}

/// Waits until the group is empty and deletes it.
fn remove_group(group: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    while fs::read_to_string(group.join("pids.current"))?.trim() != "0" {
        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
    }

    fs::remove_dir(group)
}

/// Runs in a helper process. It moves itself into new namespaces, maps the
/// current user to user 0 inside, and starts the first process of the
/// container. The new PID namespace takes effect for that child.
fn enter(group: &str, root: &str, script: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    let (uid, gid) = (getuid(), getgid());

    unshare(
        CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWUSER
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWNS
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWUTS
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWPID
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWIPC
            | CloneFlags::CLONE_NEWNET,
    )?;

    fs::write("/proc/self/setgroups", "deny")?;
    fs::write("/proc/self/uid_map", format!("0 {uid} 1"))?;
    fs::write("/proc/self/gid_map", format!("0 {gid} 1"))?;

    let status = Command::new("/proc/self/exe")
        .args(["init", group, root, script])
        .status()?;

    let Some(code) = status.code() else {
        process::exit(1);
    };

    process::exit(code);
}

/// The directories of the host that the container can see.
const SHARED: [&str; 4] = ["bin", "sbin", "lib", "usr"];

/// No source, file system type or options, for the calls to `mount` that
/// need none.
const NONE: Option<&str> = None;

/// Assembles the root file system of the container in an empty directory: a
/// tmpfs, the host's program directories, the null device, and a new /proc.
fn build_root(root: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    // Mount changes made from here on stay in this mount namespace.
    mount(NONE, "/", NONE, MsFlags::MS_REC | MsFlags::MS_PRIVATE, NONE)?;
    mount(Some("tmpfs"), root, Some("tmpfs"), MsFlags::empty(), NONE)?;

    for name in SHARED {
        let (source, target) = (Path::new("/").join(name), root.join(name));

        // On this system /bin, /sbin and /lib are symbolic links into /usr.
        if let Ok(link) = fs::read_link(&source) {
            symlink(link, target)?;

            continue;
        }

        fs::create_dir(&target)?;
        mount(
            Some(&source),
            &target,
            NONE,
            MsFlags::MS_BIND | MsFlags::MS_REC,
            NONE,
        )?;
    }

    // The container gets a /dev with the null device and nothing else.
    let null = root.join("dev/null");

    fs::create_dir(root.join("dev"))?;
    fs::write(&null, "")?;
    mount(Some("/dev/null"), &null, NONE, MsFlags::MS_BIND, NONE)?;

    let proc = root.join("proc");

    fs::create_dir(&proc)?;
    mount(Some("proc"), &proc, Some("proc"), MsFlags::empty(), NONE)?;

    Ok(())
}

/// Makes `root` the root directory of the mount namespace and detaches the
/// host's file system from it.
fn enter_root(root: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    let old = root.join("old");

    fs::create_dir(&old)?;
    pivot_root(root, &old)?;
    chdir("/")?;
    umount2("/old", MntFlags::MNT_DETACH)?;

    fs::remove_dir("/old")
}

/// Runs as process 1 of the container. It moves itself into the control
/// group, where writing 0 to `cgroup.procs` means "the writing process".
/// Then it builds and enters the root file system, sets the host name, and
/// replaces itself with a shell that runs the script.
fn initialize(group: &Path, root: &Path, script: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    fs::write(group.join("cgroup.procs"), "0")?;

    build_root(root)?;
    enter_root(root)?;
    sethostname("box")?;

    let error = Command::new("/bin/sh")
        .args(["-c", script])
        .env_clear()
        .env("PATH", "/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin")
        .exec();

    Err(error)
}

/// What the container runs.
const SCRIPT: &str = r#"echo "host name: $(hostname)"
echo "process number of the shell: $$"
echo "user number: $(id -u)"
echo "processes under /proc:" /proc/[0-9]*
echo "root directory:" /*
while read device directory type rest; do echo "mounted: $directory ($type)"; done < /proc/mounts
echo "network interfaces:" $(tail -n +3 /proc/net/dev | cut -d: -f1)
echo "effective capabilities:" $(grep CapEff /proc/self/status | cut -f2)
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 1 & echo "started a background command"; done 2>/dev/null"#;

fn hostname() -> io::Result<String> {
    Ok(gethostname()?.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
}

fn run() -> io::Result<()> {
    let group = create_group(5)?;
    let root = env::temp_dir().join(format!("box-root-{}", process::id()));

    fs::create_dir(&root)?;

    let before = hostname()?;

    let status = Command::new("/proc/self/exe")
        .arg("enter")
        .args([&group, &root])
        .arg(SCRIPT)
        .status()?;

    let Some(code) = status.code() else {
        return Err(io::Error::other("the container was ended by a signal"));
    };

    let count = refused(&group)?;

    remove_group(&group)?;
    fs::remove_dir(&root)?;

    println!("the container ended with status {code}; forks refused by its group: {count}");
    println!("host name outside unchanged: {}", before == hostname()?);

    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    let args: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();

    match args.as_slice() {
        [_, "enter", group, root, script] => enter(group, root, script),
        [_, "init", group, root, script] => initialize(Path::new(group), Path::new(root), script),
        _ => run(),
    }
}

Summary

  • A container is a process in its own namespaces, with its own root file system, inside a control group. The kernel provides the parts, and a runtime assembles them.
  • A user namespace lets an unprivileged user create the other namespaces and act as user 0 inside them.
  • The root file system is assembled inside a new mount namespace, here from a tmpfs and bind mounts, and pivot_root makes it the root directory.
  • /proc is mounted again inside the container so that it describes the new PID namespace.
  • The first process sets up the container and then calls exec, so the program it starts is process 1.
  • When process 1 of a PID namespace ends, the kernel ends the rest of the namespace.

References

  • pivot_root(2), mount_namespaces(7) and clone(2), Linux manual pages: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pivot_root.2.html
  • Open Container Initiative Runtime Specification: https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec
  • runc, the reference runtime: https://github.com/opencontainers/runc
  • L. Rice, Container Security, O’Reilly, 2020.
